posts.author: rohanpaul_ai
posts.text:
Satya Nadella officially announced that Microsoft will make its in-house Maia chips the primary inference system for its products, scaling to multiple gigawatts.

This will make it less reliant on NVIDIA hardware, and Maia 300 is meant to replace AMD chips too, not only Nvidia. The key claim is 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems

A full rack packs 96 accelerators into 167kW with 27.6TB of HBM, and Microsoft claims it delivers up to 7x the token throughput of a Maia 200 rack.

posts.author: kimmonismus
posts.text:
Now its getting interesting! Microsoft is taking on Nvidia in AI inference with a multi-gigawatt expansion of its own chips.

Starting in 2027, Microsoft plans to make Azure Maia the primary inference system for its own products and services.

Maia 200 already serves production workloads including Microsoft Copilot, running OpenAI models, Microsoft's own MAI models and open-source models.

Maia 300 begins production deployments in 2027. Microsoft expects it to deliver 40% more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU-based systems.

posts.author: The Decoder
posts.text: Microsoft plans to scale its own Maia AI chips to gigawatt levels by 2027. Microsoft will make its in-house Azure Maia chips the main AI inference system across its products starting in 2027, deploying them at multi-gigawatt scale. The upcoming Maia 300 should deliver 40 percent more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems. CEO Satya Nadella calls it "our biggest bet yet on our own silicon." posts.author: The Decoder
posts.text: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Nexus solved dozens of open math problems and actually got peer reviewed. Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Nexus solved dozens of open math problems, including nine Erdős problems two of which were unsolved for 56 years, per a study in Science. The publication comes as OpenAI faces a boycott for dumping AI proofs on GitHub without peer review. Deepmind had its results reviewed before publishing. The article Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Nexus solved dozens of open math problems and actually got peer reviewed appeared first on The Decoder .

posts.author: The Decoder
posts.text: White House reverses course and restores UK AI Safety Institute's access to frontier models. The White House has reversed course and restored the UK's AI Security Institute's early access to AI models from Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and OpenAI. In September, the Trump administration had told the companies to stop sharing their models with the British agency. Diplomatic pressure from AI Minister Kanishka Narayan led to the reversal. posts.author: rohanpaul_ai
posts.text:
The Information just reported a filmmaker-focused startup is negotiating deep access to OpenAI’s shuttered Sora video model.

Jeffrey Katzenberg, former Sora research lead Bill Peebles and ex-Dropbox CFO Sujay Jaswa co-founded that unnamed startup to build AI video for filmmakers.

Under the terms being discussed, the startup could heavily customize Sora and sell software built on it, while OpenAI would get an undisclosed equity stake.
